page: Amazon Web Services c6i.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at a clock speed of 3.5 GHz. It provisions 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading and dedicated CPU allocation. Hardware cache includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a 54 MB L3 cache pool. The configuration features 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, delivering a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results reflect balanced single-thread capability alongside constraints typical of a 4-vCPU footprint. Single-core evaluations, including stress-ng at 1889.38 and Geekbench at 1603.0, sit in the median performance tier, reinforced by hardware support for AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic instruction sets like AES and SHA-NI. Multi-core performance scales in line with its two physical cores, scoring 3436.0 in Geekbench and 5869.97 in PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth reaches 29.7 GB/sec read and 24.32 GB/sec write on large blocks. Application benchmarks show capable static web serving throughput at 6.57 GB/sec, while low-parameter model inference reaches 96.4 tokens per second for small-scale text generation.

From an efficiency standpoint, the c6i.xlarge eliminates unneeded memory allocation to reduce resource spend for compute-bound tasks. The key architectural tradeoffs include the modest 8.0 GB memory ceiling, which limits memory-intensive caching, and the complete reliance on network-attached storage. The instance is well matched for horizontally scalable compute tasks, static web servers, distributed batch processing, and CI/CD compilation workloads.
